title: Operations: real health check, structured logs with an error-reporting hook, backups, hibernating realtime
goal: Know when the service is broken, be able to restore an agency's data, and stop paying for idle live connections.
why: /health returns a static database: connected (backend/src/index.ts ~158); there is no [observability], no error tracking, about 219 bare console calls, no backup or export job; durable-objects/realtime.ts keeps sessions in memory with addEventListener handlers, so it cannot hibernate (cost model item 7).
steps: utils/logger.ts: log(level, event, fields) writing one JSON line (ts, level, event, requestId, tenantId, userId, path, ms) via console; a Hono middleware in index.ts assigns requestId (crypto.randomUUID or cf-ray), times the request and logs one line per request (replacing hono/logger). Never log bodies, tokens, passwords or phone numbers.

services/error-reporter.ts: ErrorReporter interface with ConsoleReporter (default) and an HTTP reporter that posts a Sentry-compatible envelope to ERROR_REPORTER_DSN when set (fetch, fire-and-forget with waitUntil); app.onError and the queue/scheduled handlers call it with requestId and tenantId.

Health: /api/v1/health stays cheap and public (version, time); /api/v1/health/deep (super admin token or HEALTH_TOKEN header) checks MASTER_DB SELECT 1, KV get/put on a health key, R2 head of a health object, each with latency and ok flag, 503 when any fails. The super admin system-health page can call it later.

Realtime DO hibernation: use state.acceptWebSocket(ws, tags) with webSocketMessage / webSocketClose / webSocketError class handlers, store per-socket data with serializeAttachment, list sockets with state.getWebSockets(tag) when broadcasting, and set state.setWebSocketAutoResponse(new WebSocketRequestResponsePair("ping", "pong")) so the desktop's 30-second ping does not wake the object. Check the desktop ping payload (grep realtime-provider.tsx) and match it exactly; do not change the desktop.

Backups: docs/ops/BACKUPS.md explains D1 Time Travel (30 days on Workers Paid, restore per database) as the primary restore path and a weekly logical export: backend/scripts/backup-tenants.mjs (--local|--remote --env, --out dir) runs `wrangler d1 export <db> --output <file>.sql` for master and every tenant DB from the generated config, gzips, and (remote) uploads to an R2 bucket travelcrm-backups via `wrangler r2 object put`; --dry-run prints the plan. Locally prove it with --local against fix-stack multi state.
Generated config (R103) already sets [observability] enabled = true; confirm and note head_sampling_rate 1 in the base file.

Rate limiting off KV (found when merging R106, 2026-10-14): backend/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts counts requests with a KV read + KV put on every /api/* request (fail-open). KV allows about one write per second per key and bills per write, so counts are inaccurate under load and cost grows with traffic. Move apiRateLimit and uploadRateLimit to the Cloudflare Workers Rate Limiting binding (declared through the generated wrangler config from R103; verify the current binding syntax and limits on developers.cloudflare.com before writing it) and keep the KV path only for the low-volume login lockout. Local and test runs keep an in-memory fallback.
tests: backend/test/health.test.ts: /health public; /health/deep without token -> 401; with token -> 200 and three checks; with a broken KV stub -> 503.

backend/test/realtime-socket.test.ts extended: broadcast reaches sockets accepted via acceptWebSocket, a ping gets pong without invoking webSocketMessage (assert via a counter), tenant A broadcast never reaches tenant B sockets.
backup-tenants.mjs --local --dry-run lists master and pool DBs; --local writes .sql files (record sizes in report).
acceptance: One JSON log line per request with requestId; no secrets in logs (grep test output).
Deep health reflects real dependency state (test).
Realtime uses the hibernation API (code review + test).
No KV write happens on an ordinary authenticated API request (test with a KV spy).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)

node desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs up --slot 1 --reset-db --multi --no-build && node backend/scripts/backup-tenants.mjs --local --out %TEMP%/tcrm-backup && node desktop/scripts/fix-stack.mjs down --slot 1
cd desktop && E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3100 E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8787/api/v1 npx playwright test e2e/notifications.spec.ts e2e/communication-inbox.spec.ts
goLiveVerify: Time Travel restore rehearsal on staging; backup job scheduled (GitHub Action or operator cron) and an R2 lifecycle rule; error-reporting DSN if the owner wants Sentry; dashboard alerts on 5xx rate.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.
R110 runs in parallel and must not touch index.ts; you own index.ts in this step.
In bash on Windows, %TEMP% does not expand; use $TEMP or an absolute scratch path.
